question: Describe the location of the three subatomic particles
answer: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus; electrons orbit in shells around the nucleus.

question: Compare the number of electrons in a sodium atom, sodium ion and a neon atom
answer: Sodium atom - 11 electrons; Sodium ion - 10 electrons; Neon atom - 10 electrons

question: Describe how a fluorine ion forms
answer: A fluorine atom gains 1 electron to form a fluorine ion with a -1 charge with a full outer electron shell.

question: Describe how a magnesium ion forms
answer: A magnesium atom loses 2 electrons to form a magnesium ion with a +2 charge with an empty outer election shell.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of ionic compounds
answer: High melting and boiling point; Do NOT conduct electricity when solid; Conduct electricity when molten or aqueous

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a hydrogen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles representing hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in the intersection.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a chlorine molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in the intersection, and 6 outer non-bonding electrons on each chlorine atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an oxygen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place two shared pairs of electrons (two dots, two crosses forming a double bond) in the intersection, and 4 non-bonding electrons on each oxygen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a nitrogen molecule
answer: Draw two overlapping circles; place three shared pairs of electrons (three dots, three crosses forming a triple bond) in the intersection, and 2 non-bonding electrons on each nitrogen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a methane molecule
answer: Draw a central carbon atom overlapping with four surrounding hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons (one dot, one cross) in each overlapping region.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a carbon dioxide molecule
answer: Draw a central carbon atom overlapping with two oxygen atoms on either side; place two shared pairs of electrons in each overlapping region (forming two double bonds).

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an ammonia molecule
answer: Draw a central nitrogen atom overlapping with three hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, and one non-bonding lone pair on the nitrogen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of an oxygen difluoride molecule
answer: Draw a central oxygen atom overlapping with two fluorine atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, two lone pairs on oxygen, and three lone pairs on each fluorine.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of small covalent molecules
answer: Low melting and boiling point; Do NOT conduct electricity; The larger the molecule the higher the melting and boiling point

question: Explain why bromine has a higher boiling point than chlorine
answer: The bromine atoms are larger meaning the molecules are larger. Therefore the intermolecular forces are stronger. Therefore more energy is required to break the forces. This makes the boiling point be higher.

question: Describe the 3 main properties of giant covalent structures
answer: Very high melting and boiling point; Hard; Brittle

question: Explain the limitations of the simple atomic model
answer: All particles are shown as spheres; Spheres are solid; No forces shown

question: Define 'delocalised electrons'
answer: Electrons that are free to move

question: Describe the structure of a metal
answer: Giant metallic lattice; Positive metal ions in layers; Delocalised electrons

question: Explain why metals are soft
answer: Positive ions are all the same size; Ions are in layers; Forces between the layers are weak; Layers can slide

question: Explain why metals can conduct electricity
answer: Delocalised electrons are free to move; Charge can flow through the lattice

question: Define an alloy
answer: A mixture of metals

question: Compare the structure of a metal and an alloy
answer: Metals have same-sized positive ions in layers.; Alloys have different-sized positive ions in distorted layers.; Both have delocalised electrons

question: Explain why alloys are harder than metals
answer: Alloys have positive ions with different sizes. This means that they are in distorted layers. The layers cannot slide as easily in an alloy.

question: List 6 properties of metals
answer: Conduct electricity; High melting and boiling point; Conduct thermal energy (heat); Malleable; Ductile; Lustrous / shiny

question: Explain why metals are malleable
answer: Positive ions are all the same size; Ions are in layers; Forces between the layers are weak; Layers can slide

question: Describe the 3 properties of diamond
answer: Very hard / rigid; Very high melting and boiling point; Does NOT conduct electricity

question: Explain why diamond is very hard / rigid
answer: There are 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom in a giant covalent lattice. A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds.

question: Explain why diamond has a very high melting point
answer: There are 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom in a giant covalent lattice. A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds.

question: Explain why diamond does NOT conduct electricity
answer: There are no delocalised electrons so no charge can flow through the lattice

question: Describe the structure of diamond
answer: 4 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom; Giant covalent lattice

question: Describe 3 properties of graphite
answer: Soft / slippery; Very high melting and boiling point; Does conduct electricity

question: Explain why graphite is slippery
answer: The forces between the layers are weak which require little energy to break. Therefore the layers can slide.

question: Explain why graphite is used as a lubricant
answer: The forces between the layers are weak which require little energy to break. Therefore the layers can slide.

question: Explain why graphite has a very high melting and boiling point
answer: 3 strong covalent bonds for each carbon atom.; Giant covalent lattice.; A lot of energy is required to break the covalent bonds

question: Explain why graphite as electrodes in the process of electrolysis
answer: The delocalised electrons can move and allow charge to flow through the layers.

question: Explain why graphite conducts electricity
answer: The delocalised electrons can move and allow charge to flow through the layers.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a water molecule (H2O).
answer: Draw a central oxygen atom overlapping with two hydrogen atoms; place one shared pair of electrons in each overlapping region, and two non-bonding lone pairs on the oxygen atom.

question: Describe how to draw the dot-and-cross diagram of a hydrogen chloride molecule (HCl).
answer: Draw an overlapping carbon/hydrogen or hydrogen/chlorine region; place one shared pair of electrons in the intersection, and 6 non-bonding outer electrons on the chlorine atom.

question: Describe how an oxide ion (O2-) forms from an oxygen atom.
answer: An oxygen atom gains 2 electrons to form an oxide ion with a -2 charge.

question: Describe how a calcium ion (Ca2+) forms from a calcium atom.
answer: A calcium atom loses 2 electrons to form a calcium ion with a +2 charge.

question: Describe how sodium and chlorine react to form sodium chloride in terms of electron transfer.
answer: Sodium loses 1 outer electron to form a Na+ ion; chlorine gains that 1 electron to form a Cl- ion; oppositely charged ions attract via strong electrostatic forces.

question: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons (OIL RIG).
answer: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; Reduction is the gain of electrons.

question: Write the half-equation for the formation of a magnesium ion from a magnesium atom during oxidation.
answer: Mg ➔ Mg2+ + 2e-

question: Write the half-equation for the formation of a fluoride ion from a fluorine molecule during reduction.
Explain why magnesium undergoes oxidation when reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.
answer: Magnesium loses 2 electrons from its outer shell to form a Mg2+ ion (oxidation is the loss of electrons).

question: Explain why oxygen undergoes reduction when reacting with sodium to form sodium oxide.
answer: Oxygen gains 2 electrons into its outer shell to form an O2- ion (reduction is the gain of electrons).

question: Explain why small covalent molecules (such as water or methane) generally have low melting points.
answer: They have weak intermolecular forces between molecules that require very little energy to break, even though the covalent bonds within molecules are strong.

question: Explain the trend in boiling points as the molecular size of alkanes/covalent molecules increases.
answer: As molecular size increases, the strength of the intermolecular forces increases, so more energy is required to overcome them, resulting in higher boiling points.

question: Explain why magnesium oxide (MgO) has a significantly higher melting point than sodium chloride (NaCl).
answer: MgO contains doubly charged ions (Mg2+ and O2-) whereas NaCl contains singly charged ions (Na+ and Cl-); the stronger electrostatic forces between higher-charged ions require much more energy to break.

question: Compare the electrical conductivity of solid sodium chloride versus molten sodium chloride.
answer: Solid NaCl cannot conduct electricity because its ions are fixed in a rigid lattice and cannot move; molten NaCl conducts electricity because the ionic lattice breaks down, leaving ions free to move and carry charge.

question: Compare the electrical conductivity of an ionic compound in aqueous solution with a simple covalent compound like sucrose in water.
answer: An aqueous ionic compound conducts electricity because its dissolved ions are free to move and carry charge; sucrose does not conduct electricity because simple covalent molecules are uncharged.

question: Explain why polymers have higher melting points than small covalent molecules like methane.
answer: Polymer molecules are much larger, so the total intermolecular forces between the long chains are much stronger and require more energy to overcome.

question: Explain why covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity in any state.
answer: Simple covalent molecules do not contain free-moving ions or delocalised electrons, so there are no charged particles available to carry electrical current.

question: Compare what happens to the structure of sodium chloride when it melts and ice when it melts.
answer: Melting NaCl breaks strong ionic bonds between Na+ and Cl- ions; melting ice only breaks weak intermolecular forces between water molecules (covalent bonds remain intact).

question: Explain why halogens further down Group 7 (e.g., iodine vs. fluorine) are solids rather than gases at room temperature.
answer: Molecules become larger down Group 7, increasing the strength of intermolecular forces, so more energy is needed to separate iodine molecules than fluorine molecules.
